items.title: Coherent Is the Real Winner of Huang’s Return. Nvidia Paid $2 Billion for Its Stock
items.summary: Key TakeawaysCoherent shares jumped 15% after Nvidia’s board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, a week after Coherent fell 9% on Nvidia’s leadership turmoil. Nvidia paid $2 billion for Coherent stock in March and is the lead customer for the co-packaged optics Coherent expects to start selling in the December 2026 quarter.

items.title: CoreWeave, Nebius lead neocloud stocks higher as Jensen Huang's Nvidia return lifts AI trade
items.summary: CoreWeave and Nebius shares soared on Monday as CEO Jensen Huang returned to Nvidia, a major backer of the AI trade.

items.title: Keysight Surges 10.4% in Tech Rally Led by Nvidia on Monday
items.summary: Keysight rose 10.4% as tech stocks rallied after Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, according to GuruFocus.

items.title: Applied Optoelectronics and Lumentum Soar 22% as Jensen Huang’s Return to NVIDIA Sparks AI Optics Rebound; Coherent Jumps 19%
items.summary: One boardroom announcement sent three AI optics suppliers surging after a brutal month of selling. Behind the rally sit a pending stock sale, an open investigation, and a question about which of these names can keep the momentum.

items.title: Fabrinet Stock Gets An AI Infrastructure Boost
items.summary: Fabrinet has been swept up in renewed interest in AI infrastructure after Coherent announced a US$2b share repurchase plan and Anthropic completed its IPO, which together refocused attention on suppliers tied to data center and telecommunications build outs. The fresh enthusiasm around AI related hardware highlights how Fabrinet’s role in optical packaging and manufacturing for high performance compute and networking can become more central as customers scale out capacity. items.title: Ken Fisher and 12 Other Big Funds Sold Coherent Last Quarter, While 14 Bought. Who’s Right?
items.summary: Key TakeawaysOf the 460 big funds that have filed 13Fs for the September quarter, 14 bought Coherent and 13 sold, including Ken Fisher’s Fisher Investments, which cut its stake 49%. The biggest seller, Electron Capital Partners, sold all of its Coherent and Keysight shares.
